text:
incident-bot: :rotating_light: Paging oncall: prod model-load failures detected on serving-cluster-us-east-1 (high error rate, 35% model-load errors in last 2m). Alert id: 1801256789

oncall-shaun: Acked. I'm jumping in. Launching call — joining in 60s. Zoom: https://zoom.company/incident/1801256789

sre-lina: I'm on logs. Seeing repeated failures during model Warmup/Load on node g4dn-12. Errors: CUDA OOM at load and a couple of deserialization failures.

runtime-jay: Copy. Which models? Any recent rollouts?

sre-lina: It looks tied to model: open-quant-13b-v2 (recent canary deployed 45m ago). Canary completed, was promoting to 20% traffic.

ml-platform-raj: That matches the rollout window. We pushed a new quantized artifact that changed activation memory layout. Could be incompatible with the kernel selection path.

infra-jen: Node flaps observed — kubelet restarted on g4dn-12-azb yesterday 23:00 UTC, but healthy now. Might be unrelated.

oncall-shaun: Priorities: 1) mitigate customer impact (route traffic away), 2) gather evidence (logs + stack traces), 3) attempt safe rollback/canary pause.

runtime-jay: Mitigation plan: toggle routing to fallback model variant (open-quant-13b-v1) for requests that hit warmup errors. I can push a routing rule now. Need approval to divert 100% canary traffic to v1.

oncall-shaun: Do it. :thumbsup:

runtime-jay: Pushing rule...

deploy-bot: Routing change applied: traffic for model open-quant-13b routed to variant v1 for canary and 10% of prod. (change-id: rc-1801256789-1)

customer-ops-amy: Heads up — Oauth customer-svc reports 503s for some users; starting status page message draft.

infra-jen: While routing change goes, I'm restarting the affected pod to collect a cold-start log. kubectl exec -n inference svc/open-quant-13b -- /bin/sh -c 'cat /var/log/model-loader.log'

sre-lina: Paste of the last error (truncated):
```
2026-03-15T10:22:11Z ERROR model_loader: failed to allocate GPU memory: CUDA error: out of memory when allocating 2147483648 bytes
2026-03-15T10:22:11Z ERROR model_loader: deserialize failed: unexpected EOF while reading tensor metadata
2026-03-15T10:22:12Z ERROR runtime: compile timeout: Triton compile exceeded 120s, aborting
Traceback (most recent call last):
  File "/opt/rw/runtime/loader.py", line 412, in load_model
    init_weights()
  File "/opt/rw/runtime/loader.py", line 291, in init_weights
    buf = torch.deserialize(f)
EOFError: Ran out of input
```

runtime-jay: That first line looks like a large contiguous allocation attempt (~2GB). Our new quantization layout tries to mmap a huge tensor in one chunk. Could be fragmentation + smaller max alloc available.

ml-platform-raj: Also seeing JIT compile spikes — Triton kernels sometimes take >120s on that node. We have a compile timeout guard that aborts. There's a recent env override that reduced COMPILE_TIMEOUT from 300 to 120s for faster failure feedback; might be too aggressive.

oncall-shaun: Can we temporarily increase COMPILE_TIMEOUT to 360s for the canary pool?

runtime-jay: Yes. I can patch the deployment config for canary nodes. Do we want node-specific or cluster-wide? Prefer canary only to limit blast radius.

oncall-shaun: Do it for canary pool only. Also ask infra to drain noisy node if flapping.

infra-jen: Draining g4dn-12-azb now: kubectl drain g4dn-12-azb --ignore-daemonsets --delete-local-data. Spinning up replacement node in the pool.

deploy-bot: Config patch applied to canary pool: COMPILE_TIMEOUT=360 (change-id: rc-1801256789-2)

sre-lina: After patch, I'm seeing a successful load on a restarted pod: model warmup completed, no OOM in the last 3 minutes on that pod.

runtime-jay: Good. I'm going to roll a targeted restart for warmup pods that failed to pick up the new config: kubectl rollout restart deployment/open-quant-13b-canary -n inference

oncall-shaun: While we stabilize, set traffic to fallback variant v1 for all canary and pause further promotion. Also set autoscaler to keep an extra 2 nodes for headroom.

runtime-jay: Done: paused promotion, autoscaler min-instances+=2 for canary pool (change-id: rc-1801256789-3)

customer-ops-amy: Status page updated: "Intermittent model load errors affecting a subset of customers; mitigation in progress. Some requests may receive degraded performance as routing to fallback model occurs."

ml-platform-raj: For root cause, we should capture heap snapshots and the exact quant artifact metadata (sha, quant params). I've pulled the artifact: sha: a1b2c3d4. Quant params: group_size=32, dtype=q4_0, layout=contiguous.

sre-lina: Also collecting full GPU dmesg around failures and kernel driver version: NVIDIA driver 525.89.02, CUDA runtime 12.1. Exception pattern: OOM at initial allocation + EOF in torch.deserialize in same sequence. Looks like either file truncation during upload or loader expecting larger buffer than file contains.

runtime-jay: We observed a partial artifact upload earlier in staging last week due to S3 multipart timeout; I'll verify integrity (md5). If artifact is truncated, deserialization would EOF. If not truncated, it's likely a mismatch in serialization format.

infra-jen: Found one node with noisy IO: EBS volume had high stall times during artifact download at 10:20 UTC. That lines up with the time of the first failures. Could explain partial writes.

oncall-shaun: Summary so far for incident playbook:
- Impact: Model load errors causing 10-20% increased 5xxs for affected endpoints; some customers see degraded responses.
- Mitigation: Routed traffic to v1 fallback, increased compile timeout for canary, restarted failing pods, drained noisy node, paused promotion.
- Next: Verify artifact integrity, reproduce locally with same driver/runtime, and prepare a rollback of quantized artifact if corruption suspected.

customer-ops-amy: We have one enterprise customer (acme-inc) on a paid SLA. Reached out to account exec; they want ETA.

oncall-shaun: Tell them we're mitigated (routing to stable variant), investigating root cause, and will provide a full incident timeline within 2 hours. Keep comms concise.

ml-platform-raj: Running an integrity check: s3cmd stat s3://artifacts/open-quant-13b/a1b2c3d4 && s3cmd get --no-check-md5 --continue ... Will compare md5.

sre-lina: Repro attempt on a fresh node with same driver succeeded when using v1 artifact but failed with v2 artifact with identical error sequence (CUDA OOM + EOF). Suggest artifact corruption or wrong metadata around expected tensor sizes.

runtime-jay: If artifact is corrupted, we should immediately mark v2 as bad and rollback the artifact tag. Can we untag and force deploy v1 for all traffic?

oncall-shaun: Yes, do the rollback. Keep canary changes as staging-only until we understand compile timeout behavior.

deploy-bot: Artifact tag revert executed: open-quant-13b:latest -> v1 (change-id: rc-1801256789-4)

runtime-jay: Reverting artifact triggered a rolling restart; watching for error rate to drop.

sre-lina: Error rate dropping now. 5xxs for model endpoint down from 18% -> 2% in 8 minutes.

customer-ops-amy: Notified acme-inc with update: "Mitigation applied, routing to stable variant, investigating artifact integrity. We will follow up with root cause and timeline."

oncall-shaun: Good. Let's keep this thread for coordination. Post-incident tasks:
- ml-platform to validate artifact upload flow & checksum enforcement (owner: raj)
- runtime to add guard for large single-chunk GPU allocations (owner: jay)
- infra to monitor EBS stall times and auto-replace noisy nodes (owner: jen)
- SRE to create alert if model load deserialization EOF > 3 in 10m (owner: lina)

ml-platform-raj: Will open a PR to require S3 md5 verification on artifact upload and block promotion if checksum mismatch. ETA for PR: 3 hours.

runtime-jay: I'll add a safe-allocation path that splits huge allocations into chunks and a fallback that falls back to CPU load if GPU memory fails during warmup (drafting now).

infra-jen: I'll add EBS stall alert and a remediation runbook to replace the host.

sre-lina: Creating an incident ticket and will attach logs + timeline. Ticket: INC-2026-0421-1801256789

oncall-shaun: Closing the immediate mitigation: routing to v1 and revert applied, nodes stabilized. Keeping status page updated. Will transition to postmortem channel after timeline is collected. Thanks everyone. :heart:

incident-bot: Incident 1801256789 status: mitigated -> monitoring. Assigned owners: raj, jay, jen, lina.

deploy-bot: All change-ids referenced: rc-1801256789-1, rc-1801256789-2, rc-1801256789-3, rc-1801256789-4

oncall-shaun: If anyone finds additional regression signals, ping here or escalate to urgent. Otherwise, I'll hand this off to SRE for postmortem tomorrow.

sre-lina: Handed off to SRE oncall rotation for post-incident follow-up.

customer-ops-amy: Closing customer comms loop with acme-inc; they acknowledged and asked for final RCA in 48 hours.

(end of thread)
